params.body:
Nightwatch #19 and #13, `DecryptException: The payload is invalid.` Looking at it settled two things at once.

**The one that was reported is already fixed.** #19 was Amazonbot asking `GET /website/detail/ODM2OQ==` on 20 September. `ODM2OQ==` is plain base64 of a dealer id, from an older style of link that a crawler still has in its index, and `Crypt::decryptString` throws on it. `WebsiteController` has had `dealerIdFromHash` with a 404 since then, and its docblock names that very request. Zero occurrences in the last 24 hours. So that issue can be resolved rather than fixed again.

**The same gap was still open next door.** `DealerController` decrypts the hash straight in three public showroom routes: the screen itself, its slides, and the car-set check the screen polls. Those are exactly the routes a crawler follows and a kiosk asks for, so the same garbled address gives the same 500 — it simply has not been asked yet.

They now go through one gate that answers 404. A wrong link is not a fault of ours.

The test asks with what actually arrives: the old base64 address, a piece of path (`detail`, which is how #19 reached `website/{dealer_hash}` in the first place), and plain junk. It also asserts a proper hash still gets through, because a 404 on everything would pass just as well. Verified to bite: with the gate removed, two of the three fail.

New rule R S2-7.19.
params.title: A garbled showroom link is not found
